Proposition
[Dual-basis cosine formula] \group trigonometrySource: thurston:page-0030, thurston:page-00311. 2.6.7For projective triangle representatives $v_1,v_2,v_3$, put $\epsilon _i=v_i\cdot v_i$, $\epsilon _{ij}=\sqrt{\epsilon _i\epsilon _j}$, and $c_{ij}=c(v_i,v_j)$. If $C_{ii}=\epsilon _i$, $C_{ij}=\epsilon _{ij}c_{ij}$, and $v^1,v^2,v^3$ is the dual basis, then \[ c^{12}=\epsilon \frac{c_{13}c_{23}-c_{12}}{\sqrt{1-c_{23}^2}\sqrt{1-c_{13}^2}},\qquad \epsilon =\frac{-\epsilon _{12}\epsilon _3}{\sqrt{-\epsilon _2\epsilon _3}\sqrt{-\epsilon _1\epsilon _3}}, \] where $c^{ij}=c(v^i,v^j)$.
Proof

\sketch The dual Gram matrix is $C^{-1}$. Compute it from $-\operatorname {adj}C=(-\det C)C^{-1}$, normalize the $(1,2)$ entry, and determine its sign from the diagonal norms.

□
